lessons.title: Angles on lines, triangles and bearings
lessons.summary: Follow a transversal, explain the exterior-angle rule and read three-figure bearings.
lessons.objective: Follow a transversal, explain the exterior-angle rule and read three-figure bearings.
lessons.before: Mark the parallel lines before using a property that depends on them.
lessons.ideas:
Corresponding and alternate angles are equal on parallel lines. Vertically opposite angles are equal even when there are no parallel lines.

The outside angle is supplementary to the inside angle at that vertex. Since the triangle angles total 180°, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two other inside angles.

Measure clockwise from north and write a three-figure angle. For the reverse bearing turn through 180°, then bring the result into a full turn if necessary.
lessons.method:
Name the property when explaining a calculated angle.

Show which two interior angles you have added.

Add a leading zero to bearings below 100°.
mistakes: Angles side by side on a straight line add to 180°. They are not normally equal.
Use the two interior angles that are not at the outside angle’s vertex.
The starting place comes after the word ‘from’. Do not measure from a different point.

examples.title: Follow a transversal across parallel lines
examples.question:
Two marked parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An acute angle at the first intersection is 37°.

  1. Find the size of its alternate interior angle.

    [2]

  2. A second angle shares a straight edge with the original angle. Find this adjacent angle.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) With parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal. Locate the matching corner relative to the transversal.

\(37\) degrees

(b) Angles on the same straight line add to 180°. Subtract the given angle.

\(143\) degrees

examples.title: Find an exterior angle of a triangle
examples.question:
In a triangle the angles at A and B are 48° and 37°. Extend the side from B through C beyond C.

  1. Find the exterior angle at C next to the interior angle of the triangle.

    [2]

  2. Explain the exterior angle rule for any triangle.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) The interior angles add to 180°, so the interior angle at C is 95°.

The inside and outside angles at C form a straight angle. The exterior angle equals 48° + 37°.

\(85\) degrees

(b) Subtract the angle at C from 180° in both relationships to get the same expression.

The interior angle at C has the same supplement whether using the triangle sum or the straight line.

examples.title: Navigation at an outdoor centre
examples.question:
A gate lies 45° east of north from a meeting point.

  1. Write the three-figure bearing of the gate from the meeting point.

    [2]

  2. Write the three-figure bearing of the meeting point from the gate.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) Find north at the meeting point first. Measure clockwise to the gate.

The bearing is the small angle clockwise from north.

(b) The return direction is opposite. Turn through another 180° and subtract 360° if needed.

\(225\)°

lessons.title: Constructions and midpoints
lessons.summary: Use arcs to construct triangles and bisectors and calculate the midpoint on a coordinate grid.
lessons.objective: Use arcs to construct triangles and bisectors and calculate the midpoint on a coordinate grid.
lessons.before: A midpoint is the place halfway between the endpoints.
lessons.ideas:
Average the x values to find the midpoint’s horizontal coordinate. Average the y values to find the vertical coordinate.

Open the compass to the length from each endpoint to the missing corner. Draw the arcs from the corresponding endpoints. Their crossing gives the corner.

Make two arcs with identical openings from the segment endpoints and join the two crossings. To bisect an angle, first mark matching distances along its two arms. Draw two equal arcs from those marks and connect their interior crossing to the vertex.
lessons.method:
Keep a bracket and comma around your two coordinates.

Leave light construction arcs so your method is visible.

Use the same compass opening for each pair of equal arcs.
mistakes: Do not pair an x value with a y value when averaging.
Keep the compass at the named endpoint and measure using the correct given side.
An opening smaller than half the segment will not give two crossings.

examples.title: Find the midpoint of a segment
examples.question:
Points P and Q are \((-5,-2)\) and \((7,6)\).

  1. Find the coordinates of the midpoint M.

    [2]

  2. Describe a way to check the midpoint by looking at movements.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) The x coordinates are \(-5\) and \(7\). Add them and halve the sum.

Do the same with the two y coordinates.

\((1,2)\)

(b) A midpoint divides the segment into two equal halves in the same direction.

The horizontal move P to M should equal M to Q, and the vertical moves should also be equal.

examples.title: Construct a triangle from three lengths
examples.question:
Design triangle ABC with AB = 13 cm, AC = 7 cm and BC = 10 cm.

  1. If you draw AB first, set the compass at A. What radius will trace the possible positions of C?

    [2]

  2. Describe the straightedge-and-compass construction.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) All points at the correct distance from A sit on its compass arc. Use AC as the radius.

\(7\) cm

(b) The arc intersection lies at both of the required distances. Either side of AB gives a mirror-image construction.

Draw AB of length 13 cm. From A draw an arc with radius 7 cm. From B draw an arc with radius 10 cm. Label an arc intersection C, then join A and B to C.

examples.title: Find angle and segment bisectors
examples.question:
An angle is 106°. A separate segment XY is 8 cm long.

  1. How many degrees are between the angle bisector and either arm?

    [2]

  2. Describe how to construct the perpendicular bisector of XY.

    [2]

  3. Describe how to construct the angle bisector.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) A bisector makes two equal angles. Halve the given angle.

\(53\) degrees

(b) Both arc crossings are the same distance from X and Y. The line through them meets XY at its midpoint and at a right angle.

Make two matching arcs from X and Y, with the same compass opening greater than half XY. Join the intersections of the arcs.

(c) The first two cuts are equally far from the vertex, and the new crossing is equally far from both cuts.

From the vertex, draw one arc cutting both arms. Use each crossing as a centre for a pair of arcs of equal radius. Join the vertex to the interior crossing of these new arcs.
